chose: the tabs, the disclosures and the journal's click-to-reveal are PURE CSS (:target for tabs, radio/checkbox + ~ for detail) — the page stays script-free
over: a ~15-line JS tab switcher, which is simpler to write
no hash state, tabs as anchors that scroll
because: test/index.test.ts already asserts `doesNotMatch(html, /<script/i)` — 'the page is a readout, not an application' — and the brief's own requirement (state in the URL hash so a tab is linkable) is exactly what :target IS. A script would have forced me to delete a standing invariant to satisfy a styling brief. Cost is honest and bounded: one generated CSS rule per revealable journal entry (28 on hoist, 32 here), emitted from the same capped lists the page already carries.

chose: the Map diagram is a LAYERED REGION DAG over map.crossings — regions are boxes, one arrow per crossing, layer = longest path from a source
over: a components-and-zones diagram (map.zones is EMPTY on both dogfood targets; measured: jq '.map.zones' -> [] on hoist and 0 zones declared here)
bundling parallel crossings into one arrow per region pair, which would have needed a derived 'weakest tier of the bundle' rule
because: QUERY, re-runnable: jq -c '.map.crossings.shown[]' docs/coherence/index.json in hoist/app. The 14 crossings form a clean DAG over 9 regions: browser-client/config -> public-web -> authed-user -> {patient,storage,meter} -> {public-egress,model-provider}. That IS the drivetrain the brief asked for, and it is already recorded — no new derivation. Bundling was rejected because tier and security are per-crossing and any bundle rule invents a fact the atlas never filed.

chose: the journal timeline plots EVERY standing record via a new uncapped journal.marks (id/lane/at/news/shown), and CAPS stay where they are
over: raising CAPS.blocked/open/decisions so every mark carries its text (would put ~180 entries of prose in the page)
plotting only the 28 capped entries, so the time axis silently describes 28 of 182 records
because: MEASURED on hoist: totals are 8 blocked + 14 open + 160 decisions = 182 standing records, of which the caps carry 8+10+10 = 28. A timeline drawn from 28 of 182 is a picture of the cap, not of the history — the same green-by-absence shape this page exists to refuse. A mark is a 6px tick and costs no attention, so the cap doctrine (the cap is on your attention) is satisfied by carrying marks uncapped and TEXT capped: withheld marks render as thin hairline ticks that are not clickable, and the axis states the ratio.

chose: two hoist impasses written at 02:54Z and 03:24Z are flagged NEW against a frame that opened at 06:49Z — the timeline drew them LEFT of the frame rule and marked them news at the same time
couldBe: the instrument is wrong — the thing that PRODUCED this number, not the thing it describes

the novelty gate compares ISO strings, and git's %cI carries a numeric offset (2026-07-31T02:49:18-04:00) while journal records carry Z — so the lexicographic compare reads the offset digits as time-of-day
discriminatedBy: node -e on the two literals: string >= is true, Date.parse >= is false, and the Z-normalised frame time is 06:49:18Z

chose: the instrument was wrong: git's %cI carries a numeric offset, journal records carry Z, and the gate compared them as text
because: the two literals settle it: '2026-07-31T02:54:53.044Z' >= '2026-07-31T02:49:18-04:00' is TRUE as strings and FALSE as instants, because the lexicographic compare hits '54' vs '49' at the seconds field and never reaches the offset. The frame time normalises to 06:49:18Z. Fixed by atOrAfter(), which parses both sides and falls back to the string compare only when a stamp does not parse — so a malformed record degrades to the old behaviour rather than silently becoming not-news. The consuming project's news count went 2 impasses / 12 questions / 67 decisions -> re-measured after the fix.

chose: the novelty gate parses both stamps (atOrAfter) instead of comparing ISO text — measured: it was over-reporting 26 of 182 standing records as news
over: normalising every journal stamp to Z at write time in decisions.ts (fixes new records, leaves 321 existing ones wrong)
normalising the FRAME stamp only, at resolveFrame — the same fix spelled at one of two producers
because: QUERY, re-runnable: node src/cli.ts index --since HEAD~25 in hoist/app, read the journal line. Before: 2 new impasse(s) / 12 question(s) / 67 decision(s). After: 0 / 10 / 43. Both false impasses and 24 false decisions were written HOURS BEFORE the frame opened; git's %cI carries -04:00 and the journal carries Z, so the lexicographic compare hit the seconds field and never reached the offset. Fixed at the COMPARISON because that is where the two producers meet — a normalisation at either producer leaves the other free to hand in a different spelling tomorrow.

chose: the honesty layer is a MARK beside the title (!! N unread · ! N stale) that opens intent + frame + the sources table; it is no longer the first thing on the page
over: keeping the sources table above the fold, where it cost three sentences before the first structure
dropping the staleness sentences from the page and leaving them only at the terminal
because: measured on the page it replaced: the masthead, a one-sentence intent, a two-line frame banner and a six-row sources table occupied everything above the fold, so a reader met three STALE/UNREAD sentences before a single structure. The information is not lost — it is one click from the title, it is still the first thing formatIndexSummary prints at the terminal, and print opens every panel so the paper copy carries it inline. What changed is its RANK, not its presence.

chose: TRAJECTORY joins each boundary event's chokepoint against map.crossings by symbol, so an event prints 'serveJson  authed-user -> public-egress' in the Map's own vocabulary
over: printing the chokepoint alone, as coherence log does
adding a crossing field to StructuralView, which would make the model carry a join the render can do from data it already holds
because: the two tabs must name the same objects with the same words or they are two systems. The join key already exists and is exact: a boundary's chokepoint IS the atlas crossing's sym. Dogfooded on hoist --since HEAD~25, where 4,203 lines of churn (+2762/-1441) reduce to exactly three events — one rewired boundary, one added invariant, one added anchor — and the anchor row places itself on the diagram without the reader switching tabs.

chose: could not get the Map's diagram under 7 objects by the region count — hoist draws 9 region boxes and 14 arrows
because: the atlas records 9 distinct from/to regions across 14 crossings (jq -r '.map.crossings.shown[]|.from,.to' | sort -u | wc -l). Any grouping that got it to 7 would have to invent a coarser region taxonomy the atlas never filed, which the brief forbids. What I did instead was hold the TOP-LEVEL object count to 5 per tab (masthead, tab bar, figure, one summary line, one drill strip — counted in-browser by walking the visible children of each section) and make the figure itself teach: layered left-to-right so browser-client -> public-web -> authed-user -> {patient,storage,meter} -> {public-egress,model-provider} reads as a drivetrain in one pass. The honest statement is that the SEVEN rule holds for page objects and does not hold for the diagram's interior, which is a function of the project's own region count.

chose: index.json grew from 55KB to 85KB on hoist and the page from 61KB to 102KB, and that is accepted
over: trimming marks to the framed window only, which would make the timeline's axis a function of the frame instead of the record
because: MEASURED: the growth is journal.marks (182 text-free records, ~15KB) plus the SVG and one CSS rule per revealable entry. The page it replaced was 61KB of wall that went unread; a 102KB page where 5 objects paint first is cheaper to READ, which is the only cost this artifact is judged on. Named here so the next agent measures before assuming the marks array is the thing to cut.
